title: Plea Seeks Protest Rules, SC Issues Notice to Centre, CJP Leaders

ai.summary: The Supreme Court agreed to examine a plea by Lawyers Voice seeking uniform protest rules, citing CJP's violations of Delhi Police permissions for protests in July and October 2026.

facts.claim: The Supreme Court agreed to examine a plea by a lawyers’ body seeking directions for formulation of uniform guidelines and a standard operating procedure governing public demonstrations and protests.
facts.quote: New Delhi- The Supreme Court on Thursday agreed to examine a plea by a lawyers’ body seeking directions for formulation of uniform guidelines and a standard operating procedure governing public demonstrations and protests.

facts.claim: The petition argued that while dissent is part of democracy, protests must stay within legal bounds and avoid paralysing the capital or disrupting lawyers’ livelihoods.
facts.quote: The petition argued that while dissent is part of democracy, protests must stay within legal bounds and avoid paralysing the capital or disrupting lawyers’ livelihoods.

facts.claim: The petition referred to the protests organised by CJP during July and October, 2026.
facts.quote: The petition referred to the protests organised by CJP during July and October, 2026.

facts.claim: The Delhi Police permitted the CJP to hold a Dharna at Jantar Mantar on June 6, 2026, strictly between 10 am and 5 pm.
facts.quote: Referring to media reports, the petition said the Delhi Police, by way of a "one-time exemption", permitted the CJP to hold a Dharna at Jantar Mantar on June 6, 2026, strictly between 10 am and 5 pm on the strength of the undertaking furnished by its organisers.

facts.claim: The CJP protest was not discontinued at the expiry of the permitted hours, continuing until July 25, 2026.
facts.quote: Permission was sought and granted for a single day on June 20, 2026 again, confined to the hours between 10 am and 5 pm, but the demonstration was not discontinued at the expiry of the permitted hours, it said.

facts.claim: The CJP protest continued until July 25, 2026, during which a march towards Parliament was undertaken on July 20, 2026 without permission.
facts.quote: The sit-in is reported to have continued until July 25, 2026, a period of about thirty-five days, during which a march towards Parliament was also undertaken on July 20, 2026 without the permission of the authorities,

facts.claim: The Delhi Police refused permission for a protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10, 2026, due to insufficient notice.
facts.quote: The Delhi Police is reported to have refused permission on October 9 on the ground that the intimation had been furnished merely three days before the proposed event, as against the 10 days prescribed.

facts.claim: The Delhi Police detained about 1,500 persons on October 10, 2026 to prevent a breach of public order.
facts.quote: About 1,500 persons had to be detained by the forenoon of October 10 in order to prevent a breach of public order,

ai.background_note: The Supreme Court is addressing complaints about CJP's protest activities violating Delhi Police permissions, which have led to detentions and ongoing legal challenges.
